gaps: Raw Blender command-line use is powerful but brittle for agents because argument order matters and output is unstructured.
The Python API exposes everything needed, but agents need reproducible job manifests and safe dry-run previews before running heavy render/import jobs.
MCP provides a live/tandem path but does not replace headless batch execution for repeatable CAD-to-render jobs.
patterns: Headless Blender jobs should use `--background` and a generated Python script, with user arguments passed after `--`.
Asset import workflows should choose an operator based on file extension and emit a manifest that records source, output, collection, and render settings.
Tandem sessions should start or probe blender-mcp separately from local headless jobs so an agent can choose live inspection or repeatable automation.

novel_features.name: Runtime mode resolver
novel_features.description: Locate Blender and blender-mcp across WSL, PATH, and explicit env vars, then classify the available mode as headless, tandem, or both.
novel_features.rationale: Agents need to know whether to run background Blender, live MCP, or both before choosing a workflow.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Prevents brittle assumptions about whether Blender is a Linux binary, Windows binary under WSL, or MCP-only install.

novel_features.name: Safe headless script launcher
novel_features.description: Build and optionally execute a correct `blender --background ... --python ... -- ...` invocation with dry-run preview and JSON result capture.
novel_features.rationale: Blender command ordering is easy to get wrong; this command gives agents a repeatable envelope.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Turns arbitrary Blender Python automation into a predictable CLI primitive.

novel_features.name: CAD-to-Blender handoff manifest
novel_features.description: Turn an Onshape/export asset path into a reproducible Blender job manifest with blend output, collection, render, and turntable defaults.
novel_features.rationale: The prior Onshape CLI produces export targets; this command creates the receiving-side plan Blender needs.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Bridges CAD export reasoning into repeatable rendering and animation work.

novel_features.name: Tandem MCP session controls
novel_features.description: Start blender-mcp over stdio or HTTP, with dry-run previews and status probing for live agent/Blender collaboration.
novel_features.rationale: A serious Blender CLI should account for both user-present live sessions and unattended batch runs.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Lets an agent explicitly switch from deterministic headless jobs to live inspection and steering.

novel_features.name: Deterministic render job builders
novel_features.description: Create still and turntable render invocations with explicit engine, output, resolution, frame count, and safe dry-run support.
novel_features.rationale: Rendering is expensive and stateful; agents need previewable commands before burning GPU/CPU time.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Makes visual production reproducible instead of a one-off sequence of UI actions.

narrative.headline: Agent-native Blender automation for CAD handoff, headless rendering, turntables, and live MCP sessions.
narrative.value_prop: This CLI gives agents a reliable bridge between CAD exports and Blender: resolve the local runtime, plan a handoff manifest, run safe headless Python jobs, inspect scenes, render stills or turntables, and start blender-mcp when the user is present for tandem work.
narrative.auth_narrative: No API credentials are required. Runtime paths can be overridden with BLENDER_BIN and BLENDER_MCP_BIN.

quickstart.comment: Confirm whether headless Blender, blender-mcp, or both are available.
Create the receiving-side Blender job manifest for an exported CAD asset.
Preview a render job before running Blender.
